member.name: T:System.Tasks.Task`1
member.summary: A consumer handle for one eventual value or cancellation.
member.remarks: Obtain a task from Promise<T>.Task or an async method. Consumers cannot complete it. Expected failures belong in the result type; there is no faulted Task state. This provisional API is confined to one guest invocation. Callback methods using Func<System.Void> are described in the [callback guide](/docs/callbacks.html).
member.typeparam: The value type carried by successful completion, including Result values for expected failures.

member.name: P:System.Tasks.Task`1.State
member.summary: Gets Pending, Completed or Cancelled.
member.remarks: Completed means a value is available. Cancelled is a separate terminal state.

member.name: P:System.Tasks.Task`1.Outcome
member.summary: Gets None while pending, or Some containing Completed(value) or Cancelled.
member.remarks: Inspect the union with Raven patterns to handle cancellation explicitly. Reading this property does not wait or pump a queue.

member.name: P:System.Tasks.Task`1.IsCompleted
member.summary: Gets whether the task has reached either terminal state.
member.remarks: True for both successful completion and cancellation. Inspect State or Outcome to distinguish them.

member.name: P:System.Tasks.Task`1.IsCancelled
member.summary: Gets whether the producer cancelled the task.
member.remarks: Also used by the provisional async compiler protocol.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.Task`1.GetAwaiter
member.summary: Returns this task for the await protocol.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.Task`1.GetResult
member.summary: Reads the completed value without waiting.
member.remarks: A pending or cancelled task produces a runtime fault. Application code should normally use await or inspect Outcome.
member.returns: The value supplied by the producer.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.Task`1.OnCompleted(System.Func{System.Void})
member.summary: Schedules a callback when this task reaches a terminal state.
member.remarks: The callback is posted to the promise’s queue, never invoked inline by registration. Registering after completion or cancellation also posts it.
member.param: The callback to run on the associated queue.

member.name: T:System.Tasks.Promise`1
member.summary: Producer authority to complete or cancel one task.
member.remarks: The first successful terminal operation wins. Subsequent Complete or Cancel calls return false. Continuations are queued. This is not a thread-safe shared-memory primitive or a cancellation-token source.
member.typeparam: The value type carried by successful completion, including Result values for expected failures.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.Promise`1.#ctor
member.summary: Creates a promise on the current queue, falling back to the invocation’s default queue.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.Promise`1.#ctor(System.Tasks.TaskQueue)
member.summary: Creates a promise on an explicit queue.
member.param: The dispatcher that will receive completion and cancellation callbacks.

member.name: P:System.Tasks.Promise`1.Task
member.summary: Gets the stable consumer handle for this promise.
member.remarks: Repeated reads return the same task. The handle does not expose Complete or Cancel.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.Promise`1.Complete(`0)
member.summary: Completes a pending task with a value and posts its registered callbacks.
member.returns: True if this call completed the task; false if it was already completed or cancelled.
member.param: The task’s successful result, which may itself be a Result value.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.Promise`1.Cancel
member.summary: Cancels a pending task and posts its registered callbacks.
member.remarks: This changes the promise state. It does not stop a worker or cancel the host invocation. Awaiting a cancelled input propagates cancellation to the enclosing async task.
member.returns: True if this call cancelled the task; false if it was already completed or cancelled.

member.name: T:System.Tasks.TaskQueue
member.summary: A FIFO callback dispatcher within one guest invocation.
member.remarks: Post schedules work. Drain runs callbacks in batches until empty, including callbacks posted during dispatch. Recursive pumping produces a runtime fault. This is not a thread pool or general-purpose event loop. Callback methods using Func<System.Void> are described in the [callback guide](/docs/callbacks.html).

member.name: M:System.Tasks.TaskQueue.#ctor
member.summary: Creates an empty explicit queue.

member.name: P:System.Tasks.TaskQueue.Default
member.summary: Gets the lazily created queue for the current invocation.
member.remarks: Repeated reads within an invocation return the same queue. Normal runtime invocation pumps default-queue work after the entry point returns; isolated workers have their own invocation state.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.TaskQueue.Post(System.Func{System.Void})
member.summary: Appends a callback without executing it.
member.param: Work to execute when the queue is pumped.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.TaskQueue.Run(System.Func{System.Void})
member.summary: Runs the callback, then drains this queue.
member.remarks: Recursive pumping produces a runtime fault. While Run or Drain is active, newly constructed promises and async methods select the nearest active queue. An explicit Promise<T>(queue) selects its supplied queue instead.
member.param: Initial work to execute before queued callbacks.

member.name: M:System.Tasks.TaskQueue.Drain
member.summary: Runs queued callbacks until the queue is empty.
member.remarks: Callbacks posted by a running callback join the next batch. Recursive pumping produces a runtime fault. Runtime faults stop execution; this is not an exception recovery boundary.

member.name: T:System.Tasks.TaskState
member.summary: The observable state of a task.

member.name: F:System.Tasks.TaskState.Pending
member.summary: No value or cancellation has been published.

member.name: F:System.Tasks.TaskState.Completed
member.summary: A value is available. This state is terminal.

member.name: F:System.Tasks.TaskState.Cancelled
member.summary: The producer cancelled the task. This state is terminal.

member.name: T:System.Concurrency.Thread
member.summary: An explicit, isolated host thread with a retained completion task.
member.remarks: Development after Preview 9. Accepts an uncaptured string-to-string callback. Construction selects the completion queue but does not start work. Guest objects do not cross thread boundaries.

member.name: M:System.Concurrency.Thread.#ctor(System.Func{System.String,System.String},System.String)
member.summary: Creates an unstarted thread and its pending completion task.
member.remarks: The active TaskQueue, or the invocation default, is selected at construction. A never-started thread allocates no native thread.
member.param: A static function with no captured receiver, taking copied input text and returning result text.
Text copied into the isolated worker invocation.

member.name: P:System.Concurrency.Thread.Task
member.summary: Gets the stable task containing the callback result after thread termination.
member.remarks: Pending before Start. Successful completion includes native thread cleanup. Callback faults terminate the invocation rather than producing a faulted task.

member.name: P:System.Concurrency.Thread.IsStarted
member.summary: Gets whether native thread submission has succeeded.
member.remarks: Remains true after termination. This is not a running-state property.

member.name: M:System.Concurrency.Thread.Start
member.summary: Starts this thread once.
member.remarks: A second call faults. The callback must be static and cannot capture guest state. Completion is dispatched on the queue selected at construction; its queued join may block.

member.name: M:System.Concurrency.Thread.Run(System.Func{System.String,System.String},System.String)
member.summary: Creates and starts a dedicated thread and returns its completion task.
member.remarks: Equivalent to construction, Start, and reading Task. This is explicit thread creation, not the planned platform-selected Task.Run API.
member.param: A static function with no captured receiver, taking copied input text and returning result text.
Text copied into the isolated worker invocation.
member.returns: A task for the copied result text, completed on the selected dispatcher.

member.name: T:System.Concurrency.ThreadPool
member.summary: Provides the bounded isolated worker-pool API.
member.remarks: Development namespace after Preview 9. The current invocation owns two reusable native workers and admits at most 64 jobs across dedicated and pooled submissions.

member.name: M:System.Concurrency.ThreadPool.Queue(System.Func{System.String,System.String},System.String)
member.summary: Submits an uncaptured string-to-string callback to the invocation worker pool.
member.remarks: Input and result are copied strings. Completion uses the active or default TaskQueue. This restricted worker API does not define the future general Task.Run contract.
member.param: A static function with no captured receiver, taking copied input text and returning result text.
Text copied into the isolated worker invocation.
member.returns: A task for the copied result text, completed on the selected dispatcher.
